findings.title: Verify ignores session expiry
findings.description: Verify iterates sessions and returns a match without checking ExpiresAt, so expired tokens remain valid indefinitely despite the documented lifetime.

findings.title: BearerToken panics on malformed Authorization header
findings.description: parts[1] is accessed without checking that the header splits into at least two fields, causing an index-out-of-range panic for missing or single-token headers.

findings.title: RequireAdmin always rejects
findings.description: The condition `Role != "admin" || Role != "owner"` is true for every possible role, so no session can ever pass, including admins.

findings.title: evict deadlocks by calling Get while holding the write lock
findings.description: evict holds c.mu.Lock and calls c.Get, which acquires RLock on the same RWMutex, deadlocking the process.

findings.title: Delete does not stop or clear the scheduled timer
findings.description: The timer created in Set keeps running after deletion and may delete a later entry re-added under the same code.

findings.title: Invalid LINKD_TIMEOUT_MS is still applied
findings.description: When Atoi fails, the code logs but still assigns `time.Duration(ms)*time.Millisecond` with ms==0, overwriting the default timeout with zero.

findings.title: LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS treated as seconds
findings.description: The value is documented as milliseconds but multiplied by time.Second, making configured TTLs 1000x too long.

findings.title: LINKD_FETCH_LIMIT is parsed but ignored
findings.description: The parsed limit is discarded, so cfg.FetchLimit can never be configured and stays at its default.

findings.title: Validate always returns nil
findings.description: Even when problems are collected, the method returns nil, so bad configurations are never refused at startup.

findings.title: ExportCSV writes world-readable report despite restrictive intent
findings.description: os.WriteFile uses mode 0666, allowing every user on the host to read reports containing all owners' links.

findings.title: ArchiveAll defers Close inside the loop
findings.description: Each iteration defers f.Close until the function returns, leaking file descriptors for all owners; WriteString errors are also ignored.

findings.title: Quota map never initialized, panics on Create
findings.description: NewStore only initializes links, so s.quota is nil and the quota[owner]++ in Create panics on the first link creation.

findings.title: stats divides by zero when there are no links
findings.description: hits / int64(len(links)) panics with integer divide by zero when the store is empty.

findings.title: preview leaks the target response body
findings.description: resp.Body is never closed after reading, leaking a connection/body per preview request.

findings.title: adminQuotas can never authorize
findings.description: It checks for an X-Admin header that the middleware never sets, so the endpoint is always forbidden.

findings.title: writeJSON sets headers after WriteHeader
findings.description: w.WriteHeader is called before Content-Type (and CORS) headers are set, so they are ignored by clients.

findings.title: Resolve deletes links that have not expired
findings.description: The condition `time.Now().Before(l.ExpiresAt)` removes a link when it is still valid, inverting expiry handling.

findings.title: Rename validates 'from' twice instead of 'to'
findings.description: validateCode is called twice on from and never on to, so an invalid destination code is accepted.

findings.title: Page can slice past the last element
findings.description: end is clamped to len(all)+1 instead of len(all), then all[offset:end] may index out of range.

findings.title: SuccessRate integer division truncates to zero
findings.description: `used / len(s.links) * 100` divides first, yielding 0 for any used count below the total; the percentage is wrong.

findings.title: Delete does not return the owner's quota slot
findings.description: The quota counter is incremented in Create but never decremented, despite Delete's documented contract.

findings.title: Top sorts ascending instead of descending
findings.description: Links are sorted by Hits ascending, so the 'most followed' leaderboard returns the least followed entries.

findings.title: ByOwner uses substring match
findings.description: `strings.Contains(l.Owner, owner)` returns links whose owner merely contains the query string, not exact matches.

findings.title: Extend revives expired links
findings.description: ExpiresAt is overwritten unconditionally, contradicting the documented rule that an expired link stays expired.

findings.title: Quotas leaks the internal map
findings.description: The store's own quota map is returned directly, so callers can mutate store state.

findings.title: Import is not atomic
findings.description: Links are inserted one at a time, so a failing validation midway leaves partial state, violating the documented all-or-none contract.

findings.title: Prune reports remaining count instead of removed
findings.description: It returns len(s.links) rather than the number of removed links.

findings.title: Metrics.AddResolved uses a value receiver
findings.description: AddResolved locks a copy of the mutex, so counters are not protected and increments are lost/discarded.

findings.title: WarmCache calls wg.Add inside goroutines
findings.description: wg.Add is invoked after launching goroutines, so wg.Wait may return before all Adds occur, losing probes or triggering WaitGroup misuse panics.

findings.title: CheckTargets blocks forever after the first failure
findings.description: On an error the consumer returns immediately, but remaining goroutines still try to send on the unbuffered results channel and block forever; mustHead also returns nil on error, which client.Do dereferences and panics.

findings.title: Middleware leaks token in error response
findings.description: The unauthorized response includes the user-supplied token in the body, which can leak secrets to logs/clients.

findings.title: Authenticator sessions map is accessed concurrently without synchronization
findings.description: Issue, Verify, Revoke, and Middleware all read or mutate the shared sessions map from HTTP handler goroutines without a mutex. Concurrent map access can race or crash the process.

findings.title: Cache.Get mutates shared state while holding only a read lock
findings.description: Get deletes expired entries and updates used/hits while locked with RLock. Callers holding the read lock then perform writes, racing with writers and potentially deadlocking if followed by lock acquisition.

findings.title: Cache.Peek reads the map without synchronization
findings.description: Peek accesses m directly without any mutex. Under concurrent Set/Delete this is a data race.

findings.title: Cache.evict deadlocks by reentering the same RWMutex
findings.description: evict is called with the write lock held and then calls Get, which acquires a read lock on the same mutex. This self-deadlock occurs on any eviction.

findings.title: Cache.Delete returns while holding the lock on the miss path
findings.description: When code is absent, Delete returns before calling Unlock. The cache's mutex then stays locked forever, blocking all future operations.

findings.title: Cache.Stats reads the hit counter without synchronization
findings.description: hits is mutated by Get under lock but read unlocked by Stats, creating a data race.

findings.title: Store has no synchronization despite concurrent HTTP and janitor access
findings.description: links and quota maps are shared across request handlers and StartJanitor without any mutex. Concurrent Create, Resolve, Page, Delete, and janitor sweeps race on the maps.

findings.title: Store.Quotas returns its internal map without a copy
findings.description: The documented snapshot can be mutated by callers, bypassing any store-level synchronization and racing with store updates.

findings.title: StartJanitor mutates store internals without synchronization
findings.description: The janitor ranges over and deletes from s.links directly while handlers use the store. This races with all store operations and bypasses encapsulation.

findings.title: WarmCache calls wg.Add inside the goroutine
findings.description: wg.Add is called after the goroutine starts. Wait may return before Add occurs, dropping synchronization and racing on the WaitGroup.

findings.title: CheckTargets leaks goroutines when an early failure occurs
findings.description: The results channel is unbuffered and the function returns before draining remaining producers. Those goroutines block forever on send.

findings.title: Metrics.AddResolved uses a value receiver and does not share its mutex
findings.description: AddResolved receives Metrics by value, locking a copy of mu and incrementing a copy of resolved. Its updates are discarded and not synchronized with Snapshot.

findings.title: Resolve deletes active (non-expired) links instead of expired ones
findings.description: The expiry check is inverted: `time.Now().Before(l.ExpiresAt)` is true for live links, which are then deleted and reported not found. Any resolution of a live short link permanently destroys it, causing data loss in normal traffic.

findings.title: Session tokens generated with math/rand, not crypto/rand
findings.description: Bearer tokens are 128 bits but produced by `rand.Intn(256)` from math/rand, which is not cryptographically secure and may be predictable if state is known/recoverable. Tokens gate every endpoint, so predictability allows session forgery.

findings.title: Issued session token written to logs in plaintext
findings.description: log.Printf prints the full bearer token. Anyone with log access can impersonate the session until expiry; tokens are long-lived (12 h).

findings.title: Verify ignores session expiry
findings.description: Sessions carry ExpiresAt but Verify never checks it. Expired tokens keep working indefinitely, defeating the 12-hour lifetime and allowing revoked-by-time misuse.

findings.title: BearerToken indexes parts[1] without length check
findings.description: A malformed or missing Authorization header makes `parts[1]` panic. Although recovered per request, an attacker can force repeated 500s / log noise and probe for auth handling weaknesses.

findings.title: adminQuotas trusts client-supplied X-Admin header
findings.description: Authorization for the admin-only quota endpoint is just `r.Header.Get("X-Admin") == "true"`. Any authenticated user can set this header and read every owner's link counts. RequireAdmin exists but is never called.

findings.title: deleteLink performs no ownership/authorization check
findings.description: Despite the comment, Delete is called with only the code and no owner. Any authenticated user can delete any link by code, violating per-owner deletion.

findings.title: Path traversal in report filename via ?name=
findings.description: ExportCSV joins ExportDir with user-controlled name + '.csv' without cleaning or validating. A name like '../../etc/cron.d/x' writes outside the export dir and can clobber system files.

findings.title: Report files written world-writable (0666)
findings.description: ExportCSV writes every owner's links with mode 0666 although the comment says only the service user may read them. The file is world-readable/writable, exposing all owners' data and allowing tampering.

findings.title: Preview endpoint is SSRF (fetches user-controlled target)
findings.description: s.client.Get(target) fetches the stored target verbatim. An attacker who creates a link to http://127.0.0.1 or internal metadata addresses can make the service fetch and return internal content via /preview/{code}.

findings.title: Store.quota is nil until initialized, nil-map write panics on Create
findings.description: NewStore never initializes quota, so Create's `s.quota[owner]++` writes a nil map and panics. This is a trivial availability/DoS: every link creation crashes the request.

findings.title: Open redirect through /out?next=
findings.description: The `next` query parameter is sent straight to http.Redirect with no validation, enabling phishing via a trusted host and off-site redirect counting.

findings.title: createLink takes Owner from request body instead of session
findings.description: Although auth middleware resolves the session owner into X-Owner, the handler reads req.Owner. Attackers can attribute links to arbitrary owners, corrupting quotas and audit data.

findings.title: Insecure fallback secret when LINKD_SECRET is unset
findings.description: With env unset the service uses the hard-coded 'dev-secret-do-not-use'. Any deployment that forgets to set it shares a known secret; depending on secret usage this enables forgery.

findings.title: Permissive CORS combines wildcard origin with credentials
findings.description: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * together with Allow-Credentials: true is insecure/misconfigured and invites cross-origin authenticated reads once adjusted. Errors also echo internal details.

findings.title: ByOwner uses substring match, disclosing other owners' links
findings.description: strings.Contains(l.Owner, owner) matches substrings, so querying 'a' returns links owned by 'admin' etc. Breaks owner isolation expectations.

findings.title: Page computes end = len+1 causing out-of-range slice panic
findings.description: When offset+size exceeds length, end is set to len+1; all[offset:end] then panics. Attacker-controllable size/offset via /links can trigger repeated 500s.

findings.title: Password hashed with unsalted SHA-256
findings.description: HashPassword uses a single SHA-256 with no salt, making stored hashes vulnerable to rainbow-table/ offline cracking if the user table leaks.

findings.title: RequireAdmin condition is always true, so admin gate always denies
findings.description: Role cannot be both 'admin' and 'owner', so the `||` always triggers rejection. If wired up, no admin could pass; logic should use `&&`.
